title: The Nag Hammadi Library
author: James M. Robinson (ed)
description: The Nag Hammadi Library in English, edited by James M. Robinson as director of the Coptic Gnostic Library Project of the Institute for Antiquity and Christianity (first published 1977; revised edition 1988). It is the complete translation of the thirteen leather-bound Coptic codices discovered near Nag Hammadi in Upper Egypt in 1945, along with the related Berlin Codex texts. The fifty-odd tractates include the Gospel of Thomas, Gospel of Philip, Gospel of Truth, Apocryphon (Secret Book) of John, Hypostasis of the Archons, On the Origin of the World, Thunder: Perfect Mind, the Tripartite Tractate, Sethian works such as Zostrianos and Allogenes, Hermetic texts including the Discourse on the Eighth and Ninth, and a fragment of Plato's Republic. Each tractate has a short scholarly introduction. This collection transformed the study of Gnosticism and early Christianity and is the primary reference for the library's Gnostic holdings.
